Welcome
We are delighted that you have chosen to visit our website – a very warm welcome from all of us at Bloxham Grove Academy. We are incredibly proud of our school and we hope you get a glimpse from our website of why we feel that our community is very special.
Bloxham Grove Academy is a new special free school in Bloxham, North Oxfordshire. Our new building has first-class facilities in a rural location and provides a purpose-built and state of the art environment for our staff and student community. Over the last year, since opening in January 2024, we have grown into our building and made it a vibrant, lively and attractive place to learn and thrive.
The Academy currently has 84 students on roll and we will gradually increase our student numbers over the coming years. When full, Bloxham Grove Academy will have approximately 120 students on roll between the ages of 7 to 18, with students receiving exceptional learning experiences across Key Stages 2, 3, 4 and 5.
Students at Bloxham Grove Academy have a range of special educational needs and disabilities, including Cognition and Learning needs, Autistic Spectrum Condition, and Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs. All students have an Education, Health and Social Care plan which sets out the additional support required to meet their needs. Average class sizes are 11 students, and teaching is provided by qualified and knowledgeable staff with a high staff to student ratio (4:1).
Thank you for visiting our website – I hope you find the information useful and gives you a good feel for who we are as a community!

Art
Art is a pivotal part of our provision: students are encouraged to be creative and have fun with their work as well as learning about key artists and art movements
All students in Tate and Wallace Galleries have a weekly session of art. These sessions are linked to the theme of the term for example during Wallace Gallery’s Winter theme students create winter landscapes and during their Olympics theme they create art using the 5 Olympic rings.
Our students in Louvre Gallery can opt for the Arts Award as part of their choices.

Computing
The computing curriculum is innovative and exciting whilst meeting the particular needs of our students.
A key feature of the computing curriculum is to prepare students for work within a modern and ever-changing technological world. Lessons therefore focus on problem solving skills as well as having a significant focus on e-safety. This reflects our students being more vulnerable to online abuse and negative online activity than their peers. E-safety lessons are cyclical and in this way, we constantly revisit key aspects in order to consolidate students’ knowledge and understanding of how to keep themselves and others safe whilst enjoying online activities.
ICT skills are explored across the curriculum and our students are encouraged to practise using these skills to facilitate and enhance their learning. To achieve this goal and to ensure each student has unlimited access to online resources, online learning and to offer an alternative to writing to record work, each student has their own named device.
We use the Google domain as our learning platform however we also use other internet-based resources to ensure our students have a broad exposure to online learning.

English
Our English curriculum focuses on students acquiring the key skills of reading, writing, and speaking and listening.
We believe that all students should be encouraged to be proficient readers and writers who are able to use their literacy skills to fully access the world around them. We are also committed to encouraging our students to have a love of literature and of reading. The English curriculum therefore focuses on functional skills as well as fun.
Our English lessons encourage a love of reading. To do this we use well-chosen and appropriate texts to expand our students’ horizons as well as ensuring they are represented in the texts that we use. We use guided reading sessions in small groups to support those students who may be more reluctant to engage in reading or who are fearful of reading due to past experiences of unsuccessful engagement. Carefully curated reading books will be available in each classroom to further encourage enjoyment of reading.
To encourage cross-curricular coverage, all schemes of work detail opportunities for subject specific reading and the learning of key vocabulary. This includes features such as technical language in science, newspaper articles in PSHE and fictional accounts about historical events in Thematic Approaches to Learning.
Writing also features heavily in the English curriculum. We develop our students’ speed and accuracy of handwriting as well as encouraging them to take risks with their content choices such as expanding their vocabulary banks so their writing is fluent and interesting. We focus on the acquisition of clear and functional writing skills such as the use of a range of punctuation methods whilst at the same time incorporating creative writing and exploring students’ imaginations within their writing.
Our students have a range of communication needs which can include a lack of knowing how to contribute appropriately in social situations, poorly developed receptive or expressive language skills, and difficulty with acquiring active listening skills. Therefore, another feature of English lessons is a focus on communication in all its iterations.

Maths
The focus in maths is on numeracy skills and the application of mathematical skills in real life situations.
We recognise that, along with literacy skills, maths is a fundamental and vital life skill. An emphasis in maths lessons is therefore on understanding and applying knowledge about everyday maths such as telling the time, measurement, and using money and electronic banking systems safely.
We are keen for students to gain mastery in maths and therefore we use a bespoke learning programme designed to engage learners and provide them with enjoyable experiences. Students will be prepared with the skills necessary to consider mathematical challenges with an appropriate level of independence, developing confidence in their ability and enabling them to think and solve problems mathematically with relevant skills and knowledge.
We use appropriate resources within our bespoke curriculum such as numicon and STERN maths equipment, for example classroom clocks, where it meets the needs of our learners. We also make use of online resources such as TTRockstar, Whiterose and Google Classroom to provide interactive, individualised and engaging experiences for learners. Practical experiences across the curriculum are also planned within activities such as cooking and technology projects being developed with maths activities in mind, and use of equipment such as weighing scales, tape measures and timers.
Outline planning considers all aspects of mathematics to ensure a robust programme, and we are developing a curriculum that is geared towards functional mathematics and giving learners the opportunity to develop the skills required for further learning, skills for the workplace and independent living skills.

PE & Fitness
Physical Education and Fitness is fundamental at Bloxham Grove Academy. We want our students to have fun, learn how to respond to team sports, to learn about a range of sports and, very importantly, we want them to move about, raise their heart rates and be fit.
The PE curriculum covers several strands and encourages healthy living through physical activity, it facilitates team working and the ability to be a team player, and encourages our students to gain skills and competencies with a range of sporting activities. Through the Banbury Partnership of schools, we work with the North Oxfordshire School Sports Partnership to ensure our students can participate in inter-school sports activities. We encourage all students to explore sports to develop their understanding of how to keep themselves healthy as well as to find a sport that they enjoy.

Reading Programme
Our aim is for all our students to become confident readers who can read with accuracy, speed and fluency.
Our students have a range of reading abilities. Some students require intensive support with their phonological awareness and some are confident readers who are reading at age related competencies. Our reading strategy therefore has to be adaptive so that all our students are making progress with their reading.
We use Nessy (a research based reading programme which follows Science of Reading principles) to support our early readers and those who require a tailored phonics programme. Nessy is proving to be an essential element of our reading programme and our students’ progress with reading is evidence that this programme really works with supporting our students with their reading acquistion and confidence.
We engage with ERIC (Everyone Reading In Class) every afternoon – we aim for all members of the community to be reading during this time.
As a new school, we have invested heavily in our reading books. We have books which are aligned to our reading programme, books which support our theme of the term as well as having books to support our reading for pleasure drive.

Cooking
Our students love cooking each week!
Students learn to follow a variety of recipes, use a range of different cooking implements, explore and experiment with food from other cultures as well as learning about how to budget and put together a meal economically. Everyone has fun in cooking – it is a great space to make friendships and learn about how to communicate with each other.

Learning Outside of the Classroom
Learning Outside of the Classroom is a key area of our curriculum: we encourage our students to learn independence and enjoy being outside. We understand how positive it is for our students to be outside for their mental as well as physical wellbeing.
We offer all our students a weekly class session in our newly developed Outdoor Classroom which has a purpose built fire area and mud kitchen along with opportunities to explore nature, use tools, learn knots and build dens using man-made materials.
Warriner School Farm – Educational Visits
We feel very lucky to be able to use Warriner School’s farm. We have our own access to the farm via a gate on our school grounds to make it very easy to access this resource.
Our Key Stage 2 students visit the farm three times a year to see the seasonal changes in the autumn, spring and summer term.
Our Key Stage 3 students visit the farm and use the Forest School area three times a year to take part in the following activities: den building using natural materials, climbing trees, making and using rope swings, identifying flora and fauna.
Our Key Stage 4 students visit the farm weekly to help them achieve their Animal Care and Horticulture accreditation.
Whilst at Bloxham Grove Academy, all our students will be given the opportunity to learn the following life skills:
All our students will have many opportunities to attend educational visits during their time at Bloxham Grove Academy. Examples of these include activities such as exploring the local area (Bloxham, Banbury, Oxford); going to the Black Country Museum, The National Space Centre in Leicester, a whole school trip to the pantomime plus many activites linked to accreditations such as visiting work places.
Adventurous Activities – Residential Visits
We are very keen for all our students to experience a range of residential overnight experience. These are graded in difficulty from a 1 night campout on the school field to eventually building up to an educational visit in a European destination for our eldest students.
Gallery and Key Stage
One night camp out and cook out on the school site
Wallace Gallery (KS3)
Overnight residential at Hill End Education Centre
Louvre Gallery (KS4)
Three/four day residential at an Oxfordshire Outdoor Learning CentreOpportunity to gain a bronze Duke of Edinburgh award as part of our curriculum options.
Serpentine Gallery (KS5)
Educational Visit to a European destination.
Bike Safety (Cycle proficiency)
Water Safety (Learning how to swim)

Partnership Working
Partnership working is very important to us at Bloxham Grove Academy
We work closely with different groups of people including families and other professionals who are external to the school.
Working with Families
At Bloxham Grove Academy we believe that having secure key relationships are fundamental to the well-being, cognition and learning of each child.
We aim to create and sustain trusting relationships between children, parents and carers. Engaging families as equal, active partners helps maintain these relationships. We pride ourselves on being a warm, friendly and accessible school. We enjoy working with parents and carers to provide the best possible learning experience for our students. Using their knowledge and experience helps us to personalise the approach to learning with each student.
We have many positive comments from parents – here are just a few of them!
‘I want to express how grateful we are to Bloxham grove and your fantastic team. My son has settled so well, he is excited every morning to come to school and even when he’s had a tough day it’s not affected him wanting to come back. His learning is amazing, at the weekend he was cutting out some small jumps and the fine motor skills he has developed to enable him to do this was amazing. His writing, love of craft and cooking have all astounded us. We are so thankful to you all for helping him, he just seems to have found his place and is a much happier and content boy for it so thank you.’
‘I just wanted to thank you this is the first annual review that I’ve not come out crying or that feeling of dread, instead I’ve come out feeling joy and pride you all are amazing for what you do for my daughter and everyone at BGA’
‘I just emailing you to wish you all a very happy Christmas and thank you for making this first half term very smooth. I’ve seen a difference in my daughter already she is much more confident more happy and settled and she is in the place that she’s needed to be in for a considerable amount of time.’
This academic year we have put together a schedule of events for parents to help our partnership working; this includes formal parents’ evenings, six targeted parents workshops and informal parent coffee mornings. Please download the schedule here.
The next parent event is our Parent Workshop: Restorative Approaches which is on Wednesday, 4 December between 5.00 and 6.00 – this event is led by Charlotte Roberts, Head Teacher

Personal Development and CEIAG
At Bloxham Grove Academy we believe that personal development, behaviour and welfare is one of the most important aspects of our students’ growth. It is recognised that emotional health and wellbeing influences students’ cognitive development and this is supported throughout the whole school and championed by the Pastoral Team.
Promoting our students’ emotional health and wellbeing is paramount and we do have good working relationships with a range of external services who work with us to support individual students and their families within a multi-professional team. Such external professionals include CAMHS, SAFE, The Centre for Emotional Health, See Saw, etc.
Our Personal, Social, Emotional and Health (PSHE) and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) curriculum provides the foundation to promoting personal development throughout each student’s school career.
However, that is only the starting point for our vision and values in the personal development offer for our students. We also focus on the following aspects:
Developing:
Promoting:
Enabling:
Supporting:
Our curriculum extends beyond the academic, providing for students’ broader development and our wider work supports students to be confident, resilient and independent. Helping our students to become increasingly independent starts as soon as they join our school. This occurs both inside and outside the classroom in the following ways:
Encouraging autonomy in decision making
Accessing own classroom resources
Celebrating success and encouraging intrinsic motivation
Ensuring appropriate work experience opportunities
Supporting independent travel
We provide our secondary aged students with an effective careers programme in line with the government’s statutory guidance on careers advice that offers students the following
Unbiased careers advice

Independence & Personal Development
Independence and Personal Development
We aim for all our students to be equipped with the skills to be able to live independently and to contribute positively to society via the world of work whether with paid employment or voluntary / full time or part time.
Independence
Bloxham Grove Academy is dedicated to offering a comprehensive and well-rounded curriculum centred around personal development opportunities and preparation for adulthood. The curriculum comprises a thematic, cyclical approach to National Curriculum coverage to provide a meaningful context, allowing students to cultivate functional skills, social and emotional awareness, resilience, independence and skills for the workplace.
Personal Development
Personal development is one of our 3 fundamentals and it runs throughout the whole of our curriculum.
Personal Development: we aim to give our students lots of opportunities to foster independence and to have workplace readiness including having effective social interactions and confident life skills

Personal, Social, Heath, Economic education(PSHE) and Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
Our PSHE and RSE curriculum includes helping students to deal with critical issues they face every day such as friendships, wider relationships, emotional wellbeing and change, giving them a solid foundation for whatever challenging opportunities lie ahead, so they can face a world full of uncertainty with hope.
We offer all our students an equal opportunity to develop the skills and knowledge they need to thrive now and in the future.
We recognise that our students are growing up in an increasingly complex world and living their lives on and offline. Whilst this can present positive and exciting opportunities there are also challenges and risks. We intend for our curriculum to inform students on how to be safe and healthy, and how to manage their academic, personal and social lives in a positive way, whilst giving them the knowledge and skills to understand, challenge and engage with democratic society, through politics, the media, civil society, the economy and the law.
Our curriculum and our PSHE and RSE policy are co-constructed with parents, students and staff and ensure that all documents are relevant and understood by all.
We offer a combination of planned thematic PSHE and RSE programmes, built around a spiral curriculum of 3 core themes and delivered in twice-weekly timetabled lessons, revisiting the topics with increased complexity as the student moves through the school.

Assessment
We measure our success in a number of ways.
First and foremost we use our students’ EHCPs and their outcomes to put together measurable and realistic targets for their Termly Outcomes Plans (TOPs). This ensures their individual SEND remains central to their curriculum offer and our progress tracking.
To support our target setting and progress tracking, we use Earwig which is our new assessment and evidence collation platform. We also measure success via our in-house Emotional and Social Growth Assessment, Nessy Reading Scheme programme and Maths for Life assessments.
We use our attendance data to measure our success with students’ engagement with their curriculum offer. We also use destination data to measure the overall impact of students’ achievements and whether our curriculum has been helpful in ensuring students reach their next educational stage.

Maths
The focus in maths is on numeracy skills and the application of mathematical skills in real life situations.
We recognise that, along with literacy skills, maths is a fundamental and vital life skill. An emphasis in maths lessons is therefore on understanding and applying knowledge about everyday maths such as telling the time, measurement, and using money and electronic banking systems safely.
We are keen for students to gain mastery in maths and therefore we use a bespoke learning programme designed to engage learners and provide them with enjoyable experiences. Students will be prepared with the skills necessary to consider mathematical challenges with an appropriate level of independence, developing confidence in their ability and enabling them to think and solve problems mathematically with relevant skills and knowledge.
We use appropriate resources within our bespoke curriculum such as numicon and STERN maths equipment, for example classroom clocks, where it meets the needs of our learners. We also make use of online resources such as TTRockstar, Whiterose and Google Classroom to provide interactive, individualised and engaging experiences for learners. Practical experiences across the curriculum are also planned within activities such as cooking and technology projects being developed with maths activities in mind, and use of equipment such as weighing scales, tape measures and timers.
Outline planning considers all aspects of mathematics to ensure a robust programme, and we are developing a curriculum that is geared towards functional mathematics and giving learners the opportunity to develop the skills required for further learning, skills for the workplace and independent living skills.

SEND
As a Special School all our students have a recognised Special Educational Need or Disability.
All our students have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) which states their need as being Cognition and Learning which means they will be working significantly below age expected competencies. Some students will also have Social, Emotional and Mental Health needs (SEMH). Additional SEND includes Communication and Interaction needs (for example Autism Spectrum Condition) and Speech, Language and Communication difficulties.
Please see our admissions page for further information about our admission criteria.
